Definition: middle voice from G575 and G1562; to divest wholly oneself, or (for oneself) despoil:--put off, spoil.
BiblicalUsage: To strip off — Christ stripping the rulers and authorities bare and triumphing over them, and believers stripping off the old man with his deeds. The word is a soldier's word: take the armour off the defeated enemy, and take the old life off yourself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cross stripped my enemies before it stripped me, and that is why I can lay the old life down.
